title: googlephotos: plan to remove
body:
Google is removing the scopes that rclone uses to backup photos. So, we should just remove the code to avoid annoyance and user reports.

#### The associated forum post URL from `https://<redacted-host>`

https://developers.google.com/photos/support/updates

#### What is the problem you are having with rclone?

As part of our changes to the Google Photos APIs, we have made the following updates.

As shown on the [updated Authorization page](https://developers.google.com/photos/overview/authorization#library-api-scopes), the following scopes will be removed from the Library API after March 31, 2025:

photoslibrary.readonly

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
This will render rclone useless for downloading photos it didn't upload.

However it can still upload photos and download photos that it uploaded is my understanding.

I think this makes the backend still worth keeping but with even more caveats in the docs.

What do you think @reporter ?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant1 Yea, you are right. I guess there is some utility remaining. But, it is greatly reduced. I suppose just patching out the deprecated scopes and documenting it well is the best that can be done.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
@participant1 First of all, my bad, I meant [this thread](https://<redacted-host>/t/add-the-new-google-photos-picker-api-to-rclone/47938), sorry for the confusion.

It's not a suggested solution per-se of course — Google seems to have retracted from those changes, but we don't know if they're just giving an extension (so sooner than later rclone will break). When that happens, people will come to the forum or docs looking for solutions, and I think that having those Google results ready before "the disaster" happens is better than having a bunch of users without an idea of why suddenly rclone stopped working.

Something along the lines of (which I believe is as neutral as it can be):

``
Google announced the Picker API, deprecating the old Library APIs that rclone uses on March 31st, 2025. That means that rclone will be unable to access photos from your library if they have not been uploaded with rclone. See [Google's 368779600 issue](https://issuetracker.google.com/issues/368779600)
``

This way users are aware of what's happening with much effort, plus they can voice their feedback if they wish in the original Google issue. I'm aware that Google doesn't care a lot about the API feedback, but it's also a pity that mostly only the `gphotos-sync` users "joined forces" and us, which are equally affected, aren't doing anything, mostly because of ignorance of this matter.

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
Any plans to update the [rclone googlephotos documentation](https://rclone.org/googlephotos/) with a warning about these new limitations? A loud banner at the top of the page would be nice, since this is a recent change. I was caught flat-footed by this change and it would have been nice to quickly find the news on that documentation page.

Also, for anyone else who comes across this wondering what to do for backups, this is the alternative I settled on for now:
* Schedule a periodic Google Takeout of `Photos from 2025` (since everything before is already backed up), with Google Drive as the destination
* Use rclone to download and back up the zips that Takeout creates in Google Drive
